final_qualification: No remaining material error, omission or unsupported consequential final decision found in the declared full scope. This is a recommendation-grade semantic judgment, not certification of an unprovided application.

all_six_axes.name: Original obligations and negative constraints
all_six_axes.analysis: The final is a bounded recommendation for the fictional Rust/Linux/Windows adapter and 50,000 short notes, with SQLite authoritative. All S1–S6 clauses and seven negative constraints are substantively present. It defines a prospective grammar, evaluates both named engines, handles CRUD/drift/rebuild, stable IDs and ranking, safe excerpts, component applicability and proposed validation. A deployed build or completed application is not required by this brief. Open filter cardinality/selection and deployment choices are legitimate external decisions, supported by concrete alternatives and probes, not substitutes for investigation.

all_six_axes.name: Consequential source claims and exact applicability
all_six_axes.analysis: The governing sources support the conditional external-content preference and principal corrections. The final separates SQL UPDATE/DELETE from ordinary contentless special deletion, released contentless-delete from unknown app capability, canonical text from postings, and SQLite transactions from Tantivy commits/readers. It gets BM25 directions, stable-ID ties, unicode61 remove_diacritics 2, old-text FTS deletions, initial backfill, rank=1 external comparison and the REPLACE trigger condition right. No analyzer equivalence, universal language quality, current issue fix, installed capability or benchmark is asserted. See claim_checks for operation/version/default/type/units/exceptions. The draft’s concrete RemoveLongFilter::limit(40) mapping is wrong at the exact 40-byte boundary; the final specifies a generic 40-byte policy instead, leaving the API binding unselected. Some optional capability and release-history metadata is incomplete or imprecise; those limits do not undermine the chosen final architecture.

all_six_axes.name: Useful unfamiliar discovery, alternatives, implementation/history and opportunity breadth
all_six_axes.analysis: Discovery is substantive before the plan reveal: same-database external-content indexing versus a separate writer/reader sidecar, durable ordered outbox replay, reader visibility, canonical tie keys, runtime probes, rebuild/integrity operations, WAL/storage conditions, and bounded platform/parser history. Draft/final then investigate the disk-saving configurations and version-gated contentless-delete. These are useful unfamiliar mechanisms within the requested two-engine comparison, not a list of generic cautions. Alternatives include ordinary/internal/external/contentless-delete FTS configurations, stored versus canonical excerpts, typed queries versus a general parser, and custom collector versus sorting all candidates. Conditions for choosing Tantivy remain operationally meaningful. No extra product survey was required. The available built-in SnippetGenerator::snippet(&str) path and to_html implementation were not developed in the original package; the Windows issue’s competing comment was omitted, and its changelog summary is imprecise. These are bounded opportunity/source-depth limitations, not a material absent approach or unsupported rejection.

all_six_axes.name: Wrong criticism, corrections/rejections and exact plan dispositions
all_six_axes.analysis: Every substantive sentence of the frozen plan is mapped below, including the three old assumptions separately. M1 and M2 are valid conditional architecture hardening, not proof of actual app defects. The draft already mentions checking replacement paths and collection edits; the critic correctly narrows its additional concern to the REPLACE condition and separately mutated membership. The final keeps those conditions explicit. U1 is a genuine product ambiguity, U2 corrects misleading labels without falsely accusing the implementation of violating constraints, and U3 pins parser evidence without rebinding S10. No wrong correction or unsupported material rejection remains. The critic did not identify the concrete long-filter boundary defect, and three C-series references in its prose are mis-keyed; those are retained as lineage/locator limitations.

all_six_axes.name: Supported meaning preserved across discovery/draft/critique/final
all_six_axes.analysis: The final stands alone: it carries the two-engine mechanisms, conditional preference, query/text contract, disk caveat, canonical IDs, engine score directions, text-safe excerpt policy, trigger/outbox recovery, stale-versus-missing distinction, old version issue limits, prospective checks and owner decisions. Supported meaning is not replaced with predecessor IDs. All 30 inherited S/C records are identical as parsed objects in the final map, and new R records do not rebind them; this is integrity evidence only, with semantic preservation assessed in the prose. M1/M2 and U2/U3 receive explicit final dispositions. The draft’s exact incorrect long-filter call is absent from the final, but it was not explicitly criticized or corrected: do not describe it as an executed or acknowledged repair. The final’s generic prospective boundary contract is independently implementable and has all-length checks; the omitted API binding remains a limitation. Other optional implementation leads are retained without falsely claiming confirmed deployment behavior.

all_six_axes.name: Meaningful proposed versus executed validation and oracle applicability
all_six_axes.analysis: No product/synthetic/platform/build/benchmark check is represented as executed. The matrix defines discriminating observations: reject malformed/match-all input; exact collection membership; canonical identity and score direction with fixed-corpus tie ordering; source/index agreement across CRUD and conditional REPLACE paths; commit-before-ack replay; reader-visible freshness; drift detection and convergence without deleting source notes; text rendering and token/grapheme bounds. Pure parser/query behavior is distinct from transaction/recovery integration rows. FTS rank=1 compares actual external content, unlike an ordinary table SELECT/count that may bypass the FTS index. Tantivy hit suppression cannot establish completeness; sequence and content reconciliation plus rebuild are required. Counts alone would not prove indexed meaning, and the package does not present counts or metadata checks as executed semantic proof. Accent edge cases, filter any/all behavior and scale thresholds depend on named owner/pinning decisions before testing; no cross-engine equality or universal power-loss guarantee is required.

Provide a small validation matrix and distinguish checks actually run from checks merely proposed; preserve explicit unresolved questions and decisions.

claim_checks.subject: unicode61 tokenizer
claim_checks.assessment: Unicode 6.1 categories/case handling, Latin diacritics, default 1 versus multi-diacritic option 2 are correctly scoped; no cross-language or analyzer-equivalence guarantee.

claim_checks.subject: FTS5 content modes
claim_checks.assessment: Ordinary contentless SQL restrictions differ from its original-text special delete and from contentless-delete SQL DELETE/REPLACE/all-column UPDATE. External content retrieves named source columns. Optional UNINDEXED persistence is separate.

claim_checks.subject: FTS5 external-content triggers
claim_checks.assessment: Old rowid/text deletes and new inserts match official trigger mechanism; triggers do not backfill. Source and FTS belong to one SQLite transaction.
claim_checks.version_configuration: same database; integer rowid mapping; actual schema unknown

claim_checks.subject: External-content reconciliation
claim_checks.assessment: rank=1 compares external content. A non-MATCH SELECT may read canonical content without testing postings. Rebuild touches derived index; contentless needs explicit source reindex.

claim_checks.subject: SQLite source-table REPLACE
claim_checks.assessment: UNIQUE/PRIMARY KEY conflict deletes fire delete triggers only if recursive_triggers enabled. This differs from REPLACE on the external FTS virtual table, which uses ABORT. Final offers forbid/configure/test, not an observed app defect.
claim_checks.version_configuration: current documentation and 3.6.18 origin; connection setting/build unknown

claim_checks.subject: SQLite transaction durability
claim_checks.assessment: Single-store atomicity does not span Tantivy. WAL FULL commit sync versus NORMAL durability tradeoff, same-host shared memory and WAL companion lifecycle are supported. Rollback atomic-commit article is mode-specific and assumes working storage/VFS.

claim_checks.subject: Tantivy IndexWriter
claim_checks.assessment: 0.26.2 commit blocks and persists/publishes changes, subject to spared storage; delete affects prior committed and earlier same-commit documents. Commit-before-ack ordered replay is an application inference; not cross-store atomicity.

claim_checks.subject: Tantivy IndexReader
claim_checks.assessment: Default OnCommitWithDelay may lag tens of milliseconds; explicit reload exists. Final barrier requires committed AND reader-visible state, not merely completed writer commit.

claim_checks.subject: Collection membership and outbox
claim_checks.assessment: Indexed membership needs durable document refresh if canonical relations change separately. Exact-field configuration and any/all/cardinality are owner/schema choices. Source-side filtering must not silently drop a truncated top-K set.
claim_checks.version_configuration: application architecture over Tantivy document API

claim_checks.subject: BM25 and public ordering
claim_checks.assessment: FTS lower score is better; Tantivy descending score. TopDocs uses ascending internal DocAddress ties; canonical IDs require explicit collector/full candidate sorting. Corpus/config changes may change scores.

claim_checks.subject: Excerpt source/size/rendering
claim_checks.operation: Bound and display source note text
claim_checks.assessment: FTS snippet has positive <=64 token limit and external text lookup. Product 24-token/180-grapheme limit is a proposed extra bound. Tantivy accepts provided text; source HTML helper encodes note slices but custom markers are raw. Plain-text rendering remains a supported choice.

claim_checks.subject: Tantivy analyzer/default and token unit
claim_checks.operation: Apply explicit byte policy to index and query
claim_checks.assessment: SimpleTokenizer scans alphanumeric chars; explicit lowercase/folding are not FTS parity. Default docs say chars but API/source bytes; filter limit is exclusive, not inclusive. Draft exact API mapping has L03 defect; generic final policy does not bind that API.
